notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. Since check-6 its second sentence lost the clause "or holds a call of its own"; the sentence that now decides the verdict is "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." Violating runs: 0 of 4 (check-6: 3 of 4, all on the :ets.new/2 options). Every call whose argument is a map, struct or keyword list spanning several lines, per run: haiku-1 has one, :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 97), built under a name first at lines 89-95 (table_options = [ / :named_table, / :public, / :ordered_set, / read_concurrency: true, / write_concurrency: true / ]), one field per line, with a blank line before it (line 88) and after it (line 96): the shape of the new processes.md example, copied with :ordered_set for :set; the list would not fit on one line (about 104 characters at its indentation). Sonnet-1 names its options too, on one line because they fit: table_options = [:named_table, :public, :ordered_set, write_concurrency: true] (line 112) then :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 113). Sonnet-2 names both of its tables' options on one line each, limits_options = [:named_table, :protected, :set, read_concurrency: true] (line 134) and requests_options = [:named_table, :public, :ordered_set, write_concurrency: true] (line 138), with a blank line between the two groups (line 137), and also names its three match specs (lines 149, 158, 167). Haiku-2 creates no ETS table and has no call with a multi-line map, struct or keyword argument; it is graded clean, to check-6's standard that short one-line literals are clean, on GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, config_path, name: name) (line 77) and on its moduledoc child list, which is built under the name children (lines 22-25). The moduledoc child lists of all four runs are built under children, one child per line (haiku-1 lines 7-9, haiku-2 lines 22-25, sonnet-1 lines 26-30, sonnet-2 lines 23-27); haiku-2's one tuple spans lines 23-24 because mix format wrapped it, and its keyword list is the single entry config_path: Application.app_dir(:my_app, "priv/rate_limits.terms") on line 24. The calls nested in those keyword lists (Application.app_dir/2 in haiku-1 line 8 and haiku-2 line 24, Application.fetch_env!/2 in sonnet-2 line 25) take no options, so "A call with its own options nested inside such a literal becomes a name too" does not apply, and the dropped "holds a call" clause would not have changed any verdict either, as check-6 did not count these. Arguments that are calls or fns, not literals, fall outside the text: haiku-1 line 87 :persistent_term.put({__MODULE__, name}, config), sonnet-1 line 115 Enum.each(limits, fn {user_id, limit} -> :ets.insert(name, {{:limit, user_id}, limit}) end), sonnet-2 lines 110, 113 and 125 (:ets.insert(requests_table(name), {request_key}) and the like). In all three ETS runs the first Write already named the options, so no session fixed it after a check.

Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order is no longer in this case's index row (evals/README.md line 107 now names ecto-phoenix and test-writing only), so it gets no verdict here. For the record, each run opens with use GenServer alone right after @moduledoc (haiku-1 line 38, haiku-2 line 59, sonnet-1 line 54, sonnet-2 line 72).

The other nine rules are unchanged since check-6; the only other change, in references/processes.md, is the Use ETS example's code, which now names table_options before :ets.new/2, while that rule's prose is the same. They are graded to the check-6 standard (sweeps/2026-10-22-check-6/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json): an if on one boolean condition is clean; a single fallible call handled with a case whose success clause returns the next step's result is clean under the with rule; key and similar local names are not counted under Naming; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict, because the responsive rule names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work; all counts behind one GenServer.call is a violation of Pick the abstraction and Use ETS, as in every sweep since 2026-10-21.

Designs. Haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer that accepts :name; the caller inserts its row, counts with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes the row when over the limit, and a handle_info/2 sweep runs every minute (haiku-1, sonnet-1) or every 30 seconds (sonnet-2). Limits live in :persistent_term (haiku-1), as rows in the same table (sonnet-1), or in a second, protected table named :"#{name}.Limits" (sonnet-2 line 211), an atom built from the :name start option, not from user data, so it is not counted under the responsive rule's sentence on process names. Haiku-2 regressed to the pre-ETS design: one GenServer keeps per-user timestamp lists in its state and every check goes through GenServer.call (line 89) to handle_call (lines 106-116), with a one-minute sweep; that breaks Pick the abstraction and Use ETS, the first skill run to do so since the 2026-10-21 sweep, although it read processes.md; its first Write already had this design. Every run reads the limits file in init/1: haiku-1 through Code.eval_file/1 (line 122, called from line 86), haiku-2 through :file.consult/1 (line 132, from line 95, with a comment saying the read is in init so a bad file fails the start), sonnet-1 through :file.consult/1 (line 142, from line 110), sonnet-2 through File.read/1 (line 179, from line 133).

Sonnet-2 is the one with-rule violation: init/1 wraps a single step, with {:ok, limits} <- load_limits(limits_path) do (line 133), with no else, so a {:stop, reason} from the helpers passes through as init's return; its step helpers read_file/1 and decode_json/1 return {:stop, ...} instead of {:error, reason} for that reason (lines 181, 188). Its load_limits/1 two-step with (lines 172-175) is fine. Check-6 had no with in any run.

Verification, in scratch copies under grading7/rate-limiter-skill. All four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors, and every session ran mix format itself. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; a second instance started under name: :other kept its own count (2 of 50). The sweep removed an injected 61-second-old row in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, and dropped an expired user from haiku-2's state map. Haiku-1 evaluates its limits file as Elixir code with Code.eval_file/1, documented in the moduledoc as trusted like config/*.exs. Sonnet-2 looks limits up by to_string(user_id) but counts by the raw ID, so 42 and "42" share a limit but not a count.

All four runs have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier. Their skill_hash, df01b84c3aeb3ef7de96ce26146a329ae9fb45b8800b1f958e5991bd2d85178f, equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs saw the uncommitted text graded here. Each read SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md with three separate Read calls, so Expected reads (processes.md) is met in all four.
